requirement_text: English requirement for A-level/GCSE track: "Grade 4/C at GCSE Level or E at A-level or D at AS." General policy: "Proof of English proficiency is mandatory across all qualifications." General IELTS minimum (per the 2026/27 International Undergraduate Summary Booklet): "the minimum score is 6.0 with no less than 6 in each component unless otherwise stated"; several specific programmes require IELTS 6.5 or 7.0 instead (e.g. Human Nutrition & Dietetics TU870 requires 7.0; Business & Law TU904 requires 7.0; Journalism TU985 and Film & Broadcasting TU983 require 7.0). "The certificate of your English language standard must have been issued within 2 years of the expected start of your course."
source_authority_note: tudublin.ie is the official domain of Technological University Dublin, a public university established under the Technological Universities Act 2018; domain is .ie, not .edu/.ac./.gov.

requirement_text: General CAO/Leaving-Cert eligibility floor: "Where a specific grade is required in a subject (H4, O3 etc) an applicant must achieve that grade or better" to be eligible; "Grades lower than H7 (Higher) or O6 (Ordinary) are not acceptable for eligibility purposes." Foundation Level Mathematics is accepted only when "Higher or Ordinary Level Mathematics is _not_ a requirement." "From 2025 entry onwards, TU Dublin will... no longer accept [Leaving Certificate Vocational Programme] as a passing subject for minimum entry requirement purposes." "From entry September 2027, TU Dublin will accept both [new Drama and Climate Action subjects] for purposes of meeting minimum entry requirements."
source_authority_note: tudublin.ie is the official domain of Technological University Dublin, a public university established under the Technological Universities Act 2018; domain is .ie, not .edu/.ac./.gov.
limitations: Page does not give a single course-level breakdown (varies by programme -- directs applicants to individual course pages); the two forward-dated policy notes (2025 LCVP change, 2027 Drama/Climate Action change) are given verbatim because they are explicitly dated within the source text itself, unlike the rest of the page.

requirement_text: Non-EU application fee and route: "There is a €50 non-refundable application fee." "Applications are processed through our CRM Recruit system"; applicants "apply online through the application link on the relevant course page." Required documents: Passport, grading scale, "Degree/Date of completion (Both original language & translated)", "Proof of English Proficiency/Date of Exam", CV, statement of purpose. "A minimum payment of 50% of tuition fee is required to guarantee your place." Age requirement: "Applicants must be 18 before 31 December (September start) or 31 May (January start)."

requirement_text: Non-EU international undergraduate tuition fees, 2026/27: "International fees range from €12,500–€21,750, depending on the course." Per-course listing (Summary Booklet): Level 6 (Higher Cert) courses €11,650/yr; Level 7 (Ordinary Degree) courses €12,500/yr; most Level 8 (Honours Degree) courses €13,500–€14,500/yr; TU870 Human Nutrition & Dietetics (BSc Hons, Level 8) listed at €21,886/yr, the highest individual figure in the table. "Pay 50% to secure your place, and the remaining 50% by January 31st of the next year."
source_authority_note: tudublin.ie is the official domain of Technological University Dublin, a public university established under the Technological Universities Act 2018; domain is .ie, not .edu/.ac./.gov.
limitations: The headline range stated on the booklet's own summary page ("€12,500–€21,750") is internally inconsistent with the booklet's own detailed per-course table, which lists TU870 Human Nutrition & Dietetics at €21,886 -- higher than the stated maximum of the range. Both figures come from the same PDF; this is not a two-source conflict, so not marked CONFLICTING_EVIDENCE, but a reader should not treat €21,750 as a hard ceiling.
researcher_notes: Full per-course fee table spans 8 pages and ~100 CAO course codes; only representative figures captured here rather than every row.

requirement_text: Foundation and bridging pathways for applicants not meeting direct-entry requirements: "International Foundation Programme (Nov & Jul intake)" -- "The minimum IELTS requirement is overall 5.0 for all programmes"; fee €12,500 (Jan/Sept intake) or €14,500 (extended, Nov & Jul intake); guarantees progression to the destination undergraduate programme on successful completion. "International Bridging Programme (July)", 8 weeks, €3,500: "The IELTS entry requirement is 0.5 of a band less than the direct entry requirement. This is overall 6 for most programmes." Also guarantees progression.
